en: Now listen to part two of the interview.
zh: 现在请听访谈的第二部分。

en: Questions six to ten are based on part two of the interview.
zh: 第6至10题根据访谈的第二部分提问。

en: I see.
zh: 我明白了。

en: Is the phenomenon of parent and kids studying together at university a rare case?
zh: 父母和孩子一起上大学，这种现象少见吗？

en: I am afraid not.
zh: 恐怕并不少见。

en: Changing careers later in life is no longer a rarity, so it is not uncommon for students and their parents to be toying with the big decisions at the same time.
zh: 在人生后期转行已经不是什么稀罕事了，因此，学生和父母同时考虑重大决定也并不少见。

en: Class surveys indicate that the majority of Harvard alumni have shifted directions when it comes to their careers.
zh: 班级调查显示，大多数哈佛校友在职业发展中都曾改变方向。

en: With the financial collapse of 2008, such shifts have become more widespread.
zh: 2008年金融危机之后，这种转变变得更加普遍。

en: Students have seen their family members lose jobs or change them.
zh: 学生们见过家人失业或转行。

en: Gone is the time when you start out at a company and work there for the rest of your life.
zh: 从进入一家公司起就在那儿工作一辈子的时代，已经过去了。

en: So your mom started study again just because she wanted to change her career?
zh: 所以，你妈妈重新开始学习，就是因为她想转行吗？

en: Yes, she used to be in the real estate industry but now she wants to be a lawyer.
zh: 是的，她以前从事房地产行业，现在则想成为一名律师。

en: Does her experience affect you somewhat?
zh: 她的经历会对你产生一些影响吗？

en: Certainly.
zh: 当然。

en: Freshman Week, in one of the welcoming speeches,
zh: 新生周的一次欢迎致辞中，

en: our dean mentioned that many of us might have grown up thinking that “doctor, lawyer, teacher” were our only options.
zh: 院长提到，我们很多人可能从小就认为“医生、律师、教师”是仅有的职业选择。

en: She urged us to stick to our dreams.
zh: 她鼓励我们坚持自己的梦想。

en: But later I realized talking about passions is one thing—actually following them is another.
zh: 但后来我意识到，谈论热爱的事情是一回事，真正去追随它们则是另一回事。

en: By the time I started to think about what professional directions I might want to take,
zh: 当我开始思考自己可能会选择怎样的职业方向时，

en: I had heard “The average American changes careers seven times” so often that it was hard not to become numb to its message.
zh: “美国人平均一生会转行七次”这句话我已经听得太多，几乎对此麻木了。

en: The last thing that the enthusiastic Harvard student wants to do is to imagine moving from job to job until she lands somewhere by chance,
zh: 一个满怀热情的哈佛学生，最不愿意想象的，就是自己在不同工作间辗转，直到碰巧落在某个岗位上，

en: especially when the economy is so uncertain.
zh: 尤其是经济如此不确定的时候。

en: My mom can serve as a good example.
zh: 我妈妈就是一个很好的例子。

en: Even if she graduated from Harvard herself as a brilliant student, she had to make alterations of her career.
zh: 即使她当初也是以优异成绩从哈佛毕业，也仍然不得不调整自己的职业方向。

en: So, is your mom actually happy studying with younger students?
zh: 那么，你妈妈和年轻学生一起上课，真的开心吗？

en: Hard to say.
zh: 很难说。

en: Frustration is routine for older students, you know, who have to learn how to study all over again.
zh: 对年长的学生来说，挫败感是家常便饭，因为他们得重新学会如何学习。

en: Mom once described the experience of taking classes with students half her age after 30 years in the workforce:
zh: 妈妈曾这样描述自己工作三十年后，和年龄只有自己一半的学生一起上课的经历：

en: “What’s most challenging is that you come into class knowing how to make a cake—but you’re all there to make omelets.”
zh: “最有挑战的是，你走进教室时已经知道怎样做蛋糕了，但大家在这里学的却是做煎蛋卷。”

en: A kind of wasting time?
zh: 有种在浪费时间的感觉？

en: Exactly.
zh: 正是如此。

en: Do you think your mom has played an important role in shaping your idea of what kind of person you want to be?
zh: 你觉得，在形成自己想成为什么样的人的观念时，妈妈发挥过重要作用吗？

en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对是这样。

en: Harvard offers many resources for students who want to figure out where their future lies.
zh: 哈佛为想弄清未来方向的学生提供了许多资源。

en: Advisers, tutors, and OCS keep their doors open to help undergraduates embark on this kind of discovery.
zh: 学业导师、辅导老师和职业服务办公室都敞开大门，帮助本科生开始这样的探索。

en: One can’t find one’s passions in a booklet on summer internships or a list of possible career paths.
zh: 一个人无法仅凭一本暑期实习手册，或一张可能的职业道路清单，就找到自己的热爱。

en: It’s a gradual process that involves sharing thoughts and then coming back to them; a discussion that doesn’t always have its end goal in mind.
zh: 这是一个循序渐进的过程，需要交流想法，再回过头来思考；这样的讨论并不总是一开始就有明确的终点。

en: In the course of my time at Harvard, it has been just such a give-and-take—with professors, with friends, and with my mother—
zh: 在哈佛求学期间，正是和教授、朋友、妈妈之间这样的思想交流，

en: that has slowly shaped my ideas of who I might want to be.
zh: 慢慢塑造了我对未来想成为怎样的人的认识。

en: I really cherish the time she spent together with me at university.
zh: 我非常珍惜她和我一起在大学度过的时光。

en: Well, Maggie.
zh: 好的，玛吉。

en: Thank you very much for staying with us today.
zh: 非常感谢你今天和我们聊了这么多。

en: My pleasure.
zh: 这是我的荣幸。

en: This is the end of part two of the interview.
zh: 访谈的第二部分到此结束。

en: Questions six to ten are based on what you have just heard.
zh: 第6至10题根据你刚才听到的内容提问。

en: Question 6. Why is parent and kid studying together a common case?
zh: 第6题：为什么父母和孩子一起学习是一种常见现象？

en: Question 7. What would Maggie’s Mom like to be after college?
zh: 第7题：玛吉的妈妈大学毕业后想做什么？

en: Question 8. How does Maggie’s Mom feel about sitting in class after 30 years?
zh: 第8题：工作三十年后重返课堂，玛吉的妈妈有什么感受？

en: Question 9. What is most challenging for Maggie’s mom?
zh: 第9题：对玛吉的妈妈来说，最有挑战的是什么？

en: Question 10. How does Maggie describe the process of thinking out one’s career path?
zh: 第10题：玛吉如何描述探索自身职业道路的过程？

en: This is the end of Part 1 Listening Comprehension.
zh: 第一部分听力理解到此结束。
